newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: RESEARCH ALERT - MISC holder seen selling stake.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - MISC holder seen selling stake.

text.p: Transportation firms Diperdana Corp and Konsortium Perkapalan Bhd could be negotiating to buy some shares in Malaysian International Shipping Corp Bhd from its largest shareholder, a research report said on Friday.

Thong & Kay Hian said in a report that if rumours about the MISC share purchase prove true, Diperdana and Konsortium may be "going for a clean purchase of MISC shares from Kumpulan Wang Amanah Pencen", which owns 29.35 percent of MISC.
Kumpulan Wang is a civil servants' pension group.

The brokerage firm said this scenario may explain why shares of shipper MISC were not suspended on Thursday along with the stock of Konsortium, a land-based transportation firm, and shipper Diperdana.
Both Konsortium and Diperdana are controlled by Mirzan Mahathir, eldest son of Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad. Mirzan could not immediately be reached for comment.
A suspension of the companies' shares on Thursday revived speculation that Diperdana and Konsortium were buying into MISC. A spokesman for MISC could not immediately be reached for comment.
MISC shares were unchanged at 7.20 ringgit at midday on Friday.

Thong & Kay Hian said in its report that Konsortium/Diperdana may engage in a share swap with the pension fund, possibly at 6.50 a share for the MISC stock with Konsortium issuing new shares of its own at 14.00 ringgit a piece.

The brokerage firm further said it believes Konsortium/Diperdana will go for a smaller MISC stake of perhaps 10 percent instead of the entire 30 percent holding, as this would allow Mirzan to keep control of his 38.7 percent stake in Konsortium after the share swap.
The merger of MISC's haulage business with Konsortium/Diperdana would create the largest haulage operator in Malaysia, the report noted.
